title: Digital Finance and Corporate Investment Efficiency: Evidence from China
abstract: This paper examines how digital finance affects corporate investment efficiency using a large panel of Chinese listed firms from 2012 to 2022. We find that digital finance significantly improves investment efficiency by alleviating financing constraints and reducing information asymmetry. The effect is stronger for non-state-owned enterprises and firms in regions with weaker financial development.

title: ESG Performance and Stock Price Crash Risk: Evidence from Emerging Markets
abstract: Using a sample of firms from 12 emerging markets, we investigate whether ESG performance reduces stock price crash risk. Our results show that higher ESG scores are associated with lower crash risk, particularly in countries with weaker investor protection. The mechanism operates through improved information transparency and reduced managerial bad-news hoarding.

title: Investor Sentiment and Asset Pricing in the Chinese Stock Market
abstract: This paper constructs a composite investor sentiment index for the Chinese stock market and examines its impact on cross-sectional stock returns. We find that sentiment significantly predicts future returns, with stronger effects among small-cap stocks and during periods of high market uncertainty. The results are robust to alternative sentiment measures and sample periods.

title: Corporate Governance and Market Reaction to Earnings Announcements: Evidence from China
abstract: We examine how corporate governance quality affects the market reaction to earnings announcements using a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms. Firms with stronger governance exhibit more pronounced positive market reactions to good earnings news and more muted reactions to bad news, consistent with the view that governance quality enhances information credibility.

title: Green Finance Policy and Corporate Environmental Investment: Quasi-Natural Experiment
abstract: Using China's green finance pilot zone policy as a quasi-natural experiment, we examine whether green finance policies promote corporate environmental investment. Our difference-in-differences estimates show that firms in pilot zones significantly increase environmental investment after policy implementation, with stronger effects for state-owned enterprises and heavily polluting industries.

title: Financial Constraints and Innovation in Emerging Markets: The Role of Institutional Quality
abstract: This paper investigates how financial constraints affect corporate innovation in emerging markets, with a focus on the moderating role of institutional quality. Using firm-level data from 20 emerging economies, we find that financial constraints significantly reduce R&D investment, but this effect is attenuated in countries with stronger legal institutions and better financial development.

title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Corporate Cash Holdings: Evidence from BRICS Countries
abstract: We examine how trade policy uncertainty affects corporate cash holdings in BRICS countries. Our results show that higher trade policy uncertainty leads firms to hold more cash as a precautionary buffer. The effect is stronger for firms with higher export dependence and weaker for firms with better access to credit markets.

title: Equity Incentives and Managerial Risk-Taking: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
abstract: This paper examines the relationship between equity incentive plans and managerial risk-taking behavior in Chinese listed firms. We find that equity incentives significantly increase managerial risk-taking, particularly in non-state-owned enterprises. The effect operates through the alignment of managerial and shareholder interests, and is moderated by board independence and institutional ownership.

title: Banking Competition and Financial Inclusion in Emerging Economies
abstract: Using bank-level data from 35 emerging economies, we investigate whether banking competition promotes financial inclusion. Our results show that higher competition, measured by the Lerner index, is associated with greater financial inclusion, particularly for small businesses and low-income households. The effect is stronger in countries with better regulatory quality.

title: Geopolitical Risk and Capital Flows in Emerging Markets
abstract: This paper examines how geopolitical risk affects capital flows to emerging markets. Using a novel geopolitical risk index and quarterly data for 30 emerging economies, we find that higher geopolitical risk significantly reduces portfolio investment inflows. The effect is amplified during periods of global financial stress and for countries with weaker institutional quality.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Firm Value: Evidence from China
abstract: We examine the relationship between corporate social responsibility and firm value using a large sample of Chinese listed firms. Our results show that CSR activities significantly increase firm value, with stronger effects for firms in consumer-facing industries and regions with higher public environmental awareness. The mechanism operates through improved stakeholder relationships and reduced regulatory risk.

title: Fintech Adoption and Bank Performance in Emerging Markets
abstract: This paper investigates how fintech adoption affects traditional bank performance in emerging markets. Using data from 25 emerging economies, we find that fintech adoption initially reduces bank profitability but improves efficiency over time. Banks that proactively adopt digital technologies experience smaller performance declines and faster recovery.
